The work, photographed on site

These are our own photographs from jobs across the corridor. We have deliberately not labelled them with suburbs or client names, because we are not going to attach a property to a job without the owner saying we can.

0456 220 552

What the work looks like

Six kinds of job, and what each one leaves behind

Each photograph is of our own work. The captions describe what is in the frame rather than making a claim about where it was taken.

Residential demolition

Taken down from the top with a grapple rather than pushed over, so the material comes away in a controlled sequence and can be sorted as it falls. Residential demolition

Partial and hand demolition

Stripped back to the frame with the walls still standing. What is retained is decided and protected before the machine arrives, not during. Partial demolition

Asbestos removal

Cement sheeting taken off sheet by sheet rather than broken, by licensed asbestos removalists, with independent clearance before demolition starts. Asbestos services

Rock excavation

A cut face part way down on a Northern Beaches block. Rock is priced by the cubic metre at a rate agreed before the dig starts. Rock excavation

Cleared and levelled

What handover should look like: graded, clear, boundary fencing intact, and the disposal dockets handed over with it. Site clearing

Spoil and cartage

A truck and dog loaded at the work face. Fewer trips for the same volume is the single biggest saving available on a dig. Spoil removal and cartage

Case studies are coming. Named project pages with the suburb, the scope, the programme and the before and after photographs will be published as owners and builders give us permission to use them. We would rather have six real ones than sixty invented ones.
